newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLL-FINNISH '98 NOMINAL PAY RISES SEEN AT 2.5 PCT.
newsitem.headline: POLL-FINNISH '98 NOMINAL PAY RISES SEEN AT 2.5 PCT.

text.p: Finnish trade unions and
employers are expected to agree on nominal pay rises of around
2.5 percent for the first 12 months of a new incomes settlement
from February 1998, according to a Reuters poll.
Nearly 60 percent, or 13 of 22 dealers, analysts and
economists at banks and corporate treasuries, expected another
broad centralised pay deal, while nine respondents forecast
branch-level settlements.
Those expecting branch-level agreements forecast slightly
higher nominal pay rises than those who believed in a
centralised incomes settlement.

In September 1995, unions and employers reached a
centralised two-year pay deal with a minimun pay rise of 1.8
percent for the first 12 months from November 1995 to October
In November 1996, wages rose by 1.3 percent, and in the
beginning of this year, an extra pay rise of around 0.4 percent
was granted to low-paid employees.
The current incomes settlement expires at end-January 1998.
The poll was conducted by telephone on May 22-23 and
forecasts were collected on an anonymous basis.
Forecasts by Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque
